exec: An election authority reported a suspected attack on its website during voting; no impact is stated.
geo_basis: national commission headquarters (Putrajaya); Bernama gives only a Melaka dateline
plain: Malaysia's Election Commission said its website may be facing a cyberattack during early voting for a state election. It is working with the communications regulator; no effect on the site was reported.
summary: Malaysia's Election Commission (EC) said on 10 November, during early voting for the 16th Melaka State Election, that its website was believed to be facing a cyber attack threat, Bernama reports. Chairman Ramlan Harun said the EC is working with MCMC and other parties to strengthen the site's security, that a report went to the relevant authorities, and that he had yet to receive a full report. No impact is stated.
title: Malaysia Election Commission reports suspected cyberattack on its website during Melaka early voting

validation.note: Follow-up read Bernama (10 Nov 2026), which quotes EC chairman Ramlan Harun, so this is a 2026 event, not a recycled 2022 one; the SharkStriker tracker was removed. Malay Mail answered 403. Bernama states no impact; the official EC statement it promised was not found.

review.note: Only source is SharkStriker tracker whose own entry links a 2022 NST URL, so it may recycle the 2022 attack; no 2026 official statement found.

date_note: Bernama (10 Nov, 11:44) reports the EC announced the suspected attack earlier that day during early voting; the page gives no earlier day.
